title: SEO: Search Engine Optimization
tagline: Be found by the right people, honestly, with hands-on labs in every module
summary: Learn practical search engine optimisation: how search works, keywords and helpful content, on-page and technical SEO, links and local SEO, measurement and a three-month plan. Every module has a hands-on lab.

modules.title: How search works
modules.summary: How search engines find, store and rank pages, and why intent matters.
modules.outcome: You can explain crawling, indexing and ranking and identify the intent behind a query.
modules.intro: Search engine optimisation (SEO) is the work of making your pages easy for search engines to understand and worth showing to people. To do that well you first need a clear picture of what a search engine actually does.

topics.title: Crawl, index, rank
topics.html:
Definition

SEO. The practice of improving a website so that it appears higher in unpaid (organic) search results for searches that matter to its audience.

The three steps
StepWhat happensWhat can go wrong
CrawlAutomated bots (crawlers) follow links and read pagesNo links to the page, blocked by a rule, slow server
IndexThe engine stores and understands the contentThin, duplicate or unreadable content; marked 'do not index'
RankPages are ordered for each queryWeak match to intent, low quality or low trust

A page cannot rank if it was never crawled, and it cannot be crawled if nothing links to it. Many SEO problems are simply visibility problems earlier in this chain.

Tip

To see whether a page is indexed, search for its exact address or use the free search console tool from the search engine.

Check what you just learned

1. Which step stores and analyses pages?
  • Crawl
  • Index (correct)
  • Rank
  • Click

Indexing builds the library.
keyPoints: Search engines crawl, index and rank pages.
A page must be found and understood before it can rank.

topics.title: Search intent
topics.html:
The most important idea in modern SEO is intent: why the person typed the query. A page that matches the intent has a chance; a page that does not will not rank however well it is optimised.

Four kinds of intent
IntentExample queryBest page type
Informationalhow to remove a coffee stainGuide, article, video
Navigationalfacebook loginThe official site
Commercialbest running shoes for flat feetComparison, review
Transactionalbuy running shoes size 9Product or category page
Worked example

Reading the results

You search for 'eggless birthday cake pune' and the top results are local bakeries with order buttons.

  1. The intent is transactional and local.
  2. A long article about the history of cake would not match.
  3. A page with photos, prices, flavours and an order button would.

Answer. Look at what already ranks to learn what the engine thinks people want.

Common mistakes

  • Writing a long article for a query where people want to buy.
  • Putting a product page where people want to learn.
  • Ignoring the place in local searches.

Check what you just learned

1. 'best laptop under 50000' is mostly which intent?
  • Navigational
  • Informational only
  • Commercial (correct)
  • None

The searcher is comparing options.
keyPoints: Intent is why someone searched.
Match the page type to the intent by studying the results.

topics.title: What the results page shows
topics.html:
A results page is more than ten blue links. Understanding its parts shows where you can appear.

Parts of a results page
PartDescriptionOpportunity
Paid advertsMarked as ads at the top and bottomPay per click
Organic resultsTitle, address and descriptionGood titles and content
Local packA map with nearby businessesA complete business profile and reviews
Featured answerA short direct answerClear, concise answers to questions
Images, video, newsOther result typesGood media with descriptions

Why this matters

  • Fewer people click when the answer is shown directly, so aim to be the answer or give a reason to click.
  • Local searches reward a complete, accurate business profile.
  • The title and description decide whether a ranked page gets the click.
Watch out

Nobody can promise a first-place ranking. Rankings depend on the engine's rules, your competitors and your quality, and they change. Be sceptical of anyone who guarantees results.

Check what you just learned

1. Which part rewards a complete business profile and reviews?
  • Paid ads
  • Images
  • Featured answer
  • The local pack (correct)

Local results use profiles.

Key terms: flip and sort

Crawler
A bot that reads pages by following links
Index
The engine's stored library of pages
Rank
Position in the results
Organic
Unpaid results
Search intent
Why someone searched
keyPoints: Results include ads, organic links, local packs and answers.
No honest SEO guarantees rankings.

modules.title: Keywords and content
modules.summary: Find the phrases people use, choose the best ones and write pages that answer them well.
modules.outcome: You can research keywords, score opportunities and plan a helpful page structure.
modules.intro: Keywords are the bridge between what people type and what you offer. But modern SEO is not about repeating words; it is about covering a topic so well that the searcher needs nothing more.

topics.title: Keyword research
topics.html:
Start with the language of customers, not the language of your industry. A plumber says 'leak repair'; a customer types 'tap dripping at night'.

Where to find ideas

  1. Ask customers how they describe the problem.
  2. Use the suggestions that appear as you type in a search box.
  3. Look at the 'people also ask' questions.
  4. Use free tools from search engines to see volumes.
  5. Look at the headings of pages that already rank.
What to record for each phrase
ItemMeaning
Searches per monthHow many people look
DifficultyHow strong the competition is
IntentWhat the searcher wants
RelevanceHow well it fits what you offer

Keep a simple spreadsheet of every phrase you consider, with the page you plan to use for it. Review it every quarter: search behaviour shifts with seasons, news and new products, and a phrase that mattered last year may now be replaced by a different way of asking the same question.

Tip

A phrase with few searches but a high chance of winning and clear buying intent is often better than a huge, difficult one.

Check what you just learned

1. A keyword with low volume can still be valuable when:
  • Intent is strong and competition is low (correct)
  • It never is
  • It has many letters
  • It is capitalised

Fit and winnability matter.
keyPoints: Use the customers' words.
Record volume, difficulty, intent and relevance.

topics.title: Choosing and scoring keywords
topics.html:
Formula · A simple opportunity score

opportunity = searches × win chance ÷ difficulty

Higher searches and a better chance raise the score; tougher competition lowers it.

Which keyword to target?

Change the numbers and watch how the opportunity score changes.

Adjust Monthly searches, Win chance (percent), Difficulty (1-100) and see Opportunity score, Expected visits if you win change.

Short-tail and long-tail
TypeExampleVolumeCompetitionIntent
Short-tailcakeVery highVery highUnclear
Long-taileggless birthday cake in puneLowLowClear

Common mistakes

  • Chasing the biggest phrase and ignoring winnable ones.
  • Choosing keywords with no link to what you sell.
  • Using one page to target ten different intents.

Check what you just learned

1. Long-tail phrases are usually:
  • Higher competition
  • More specific with clearer intent (correct)
  • Always useless
  • Single words

They are specific and winnable.
keyPoints: Score keywords, then target winnable long-tail phrases first.
One main intent per page.

topics.title: Content that deserves to rank
topics.html:
Search engines aim to show helpful, reliable, people-first content. That means pages written to serve a reader, by someone who knows the subject, not pages stuffed to please a machine.

Marks of a helpful page

  • It answers the question early and completely.
  • It shows real experience or expertise, with sources where they matter.
  • It is clearly organised with one H1 and logical subheadings.
  • It is original: it says something that other pages do not.
  • It is up to date and easy to read on a phone.
  • It tells the reader what to do next.
Worked example

Title and description

Page: eggless birthday cakes in Pune.

  1. Title: Eggless Birthday Cake in Pune | Fresh Home Bakery (under 60 characters).
  2. Description: a one- or two-sentence summary with a benefit and a call to action, under about 160 characters.
  3. Each page needs its own pair.

Answer. These are the shop window of a result: they decide whether your ranking turns into a click.

Watch out

Writing with the sole aim of ranking, copying other pages or generating many thin pages is exactly what quality systems try to filter out.

Check what you just learned

1. Which is most likely to be penalised?
  • A guide with original examples
  • A clear FAQ
  • Many thin pages written only to rank (correct)
  • A well-labelled image

Thin, search-first pages are filtered.

Key terms: flip and sort

Keyword
A word or phrase people search for
Long-tail
A specific, lower-volume phrase
Difficulty
How hard it is to outrank others
Title tag
The clickable headline of a result
Meta description
The summary under the title
keyPoints: Write people-first content that answers early and completely.
Give every page a unique title and description.

modules.title: On-page and technical SEO
modules.summary: Structure pages clearly, make sites fast and mobile-friendly and help crawlers find everything.
modules.outcome: You can structure a page with headings and descriptive media, and check speed, mobile friendliness and crawlability.
modules.intro: On-page SEO is about what is on the page. Technical SEO is about whether the site works well for crawlers and visitors. They overlap, and both are mostly common sense applied carefully.

topics.title: Structuring a page
topics.html:
The parts of a well-built page
PartGuidance
Title tagUnique, under about 60 characters, includes the main phrase naturally
H1 headingOne per page; says what the page is about
Subheadings (H2, H3)Organise sections in a logical outline
Body textClear, helpful, easy to scan
ImagesDescriptive file names and alt text; compressed
Internal linksLink to related pages with descriptive words
Address (URL)Short, readable and lowercase with hyphens
Worked example

Alt text

Image of a chocolate cake with candles.

  1. Weak alt text: image1.
  2. Better alt text: eggless chocolate birthday cake with candles.
  3. Alt text helps screen-reader users first and search second.

Answer. Write alt text for people who cannot see the image.

Internal links

  • Use words that describe the destination: 'eggless cake flavours', not 'click here'.
  • Link related pages so crawlers and visitors can move between them.
  • Make sure every important page is linked from somewhere.
Tip

An outline of headings should read like a table of contents. If it does not, the page is probably unclear.

Check what you just learned

1. Good alt text is:
  • image1
  • Empty always
  • A list of keywords
  • A short description of the image (correct)

It describes what is shown.
keyPoints: Use one H1, logical subheadings, descriptive alt text and internal links.
Readable addresses help people and engines.

topics.title: Speed and mobile
topics.html:
Most searches happen on phones, often on slow connections. A slow or awkward page loses visitors before they read a word, and engines notice.

Common speed fixes
ProblemFix
Huge imagesResize and compress; use modern formats
Too many scriptsRemove the ones you do not need
No cachingLet browsers keep files they already downloaded
Everything loads at onceLoad images lower on the page only when needed
Slow hostingChoose a better server or a content delivery network

Mobile checks

  • Text readable without zooming.
  • Buttons large enough to tap.
  • No horizontal scrolling.
  • Pop-ups that do not cover the content.
  • Same important content as on a computer.
Watch out

Do not hide content on mobile that you want ranked: search engines mainly use the mobile version of your page.

Check what you just learned

1. A common first fix for a slow page is:
  • Compressing images (correct)
  • More images
  • More pop-ups
  • Longer titles

Images are often the heaviest part.
keyPoints: Fast, mobile-friendly pages keep visitors and rank better.
Compress images, trim scripts, cache and lazy-load.

topics.title: Crawlability, indexing and structure
topics.html:
Technical tools
ToolPurpose
XML sitemapA list of important pages for crawlers
robots.txtTells crawlers which areas to avoid
Canonical tagNames the main version of duplicate pages
HTTPSSecure connection; expected by users and engines
Redirects (301)Send visitors and engines to a page's new address
Structured dataLabels such as product, review or event so engines understand the page

Common mistakes

  • Blocking the whole site in robots.txt by accident.
  • Leaving a staging site open to indexing, or a live site marked 'do not index'.
  • Changing addresses without redirects, creating broken links.
  • Having many duplicate pages with no main version.
Tip

After any redesign, crawl the old and new sites and check that every old address redirects to a sensible new one.

Check what you just learned

1. A 301 redirect is used when:
  • A page is deleted for ever
  • A page has moved permanently (correct)
  • A page is slow
  • A page has a typo

It points to the new address.

Key terms: flip and sort

H1
The main heading of a page
Alt text
A text description of an image
Sitemap
A list of pages for crawlers
Canonical
The preferred version of a page
301 redirect
A permanent move
keyPoints: Sitemaps, robots rules, canonical tags, HTTPS and redirects help crawlers.
Debug missing pages step by step.

modules.title: Links, authority and local SEO
modules.summary: Earn trust through links and reviews, work with local search and avoid shortcuts that cost you later.
modules.outcome: You can describe how links signal trust, set up the basics of local SEO and tell good practice from spam.
modules.intro: Search engines treat a link from one site to another as a recommendation. But a recommendation is only worth something when it is earned. This module covers how to earn trust, locally and online, and how to avoid the shortcuts that backfire.

topics.title: Links as recommendations
topics.html:
Definition

Backlink. A link from another website to yours. Links from relevant, trusted sites are worth far more than many links from poor ones.

Good and poor links
GoodPoor
From a relevant, respected siteFrom unrelated or spammy pages
Earned because your content is usefulBought or exchanged in bulk
Placed naturally in an articleHidden in a footer or comments
Varied, descriptive anchor textThe same keyword phrase every time

Ethical ways to earn links

  • Publish original research, guides or tools others want to cite.
  • Be useful to journalists and bloggers in your field.
  • Get listed in genuine industry directories and associations.
  • Sponsor or contribute to local events and organisations.
  • Fix broken links on sites by offering your relevant page (politely).
Watch out

Buying links, running link farms and hidden manipulation can bring a penalty that removes your site from results. Recovery can take months.

Check what you just learned

1. Which link is most valuable?
  • From a bulk-bought directory
  • From a hidden footer
  • From a respected relevant site that cites your guide (correct)
  • From a spam comment

Relevance and trust matter.
keyPoints: Links are recommendations; quality and relevance beat quantity.
Earn links by being useful; do not buy them.

topics.title: Local SEO
topics.html:
For shops, clinics, restaurants and services with a place, local search is often the biggest opportunity. The local pack shows a map and a few nearby businesses.

Local ranking foundations
FactorHow to improve it
RelevanceChoose the right categories and describe services clearly
DistanceYou cannot move, but you can make sure your address is accurate
ProminenceReviews, mentions and a strong website

The local checklist

  1. Claim and complete your business profile: name, address, phone, hours, photos.
  2. Keep your name, address and phone number identical everywhere.
  3. Ask happy customers for honest reviews and reply to all of them.
  4. Create pages for each service and each area you serve.
  5. Add the city to titles and headings where it is natural.

Common mistakes

  • Different phone numbers or addresses on different sites.
  • Creating fake locations to appear in more areas.
  • Buying reviews or writing your own.

Check what you just learned

1. Which is a legitimate way to improve local ranking?
  • Fake reviews
  • Hiding your phone number
  • Creating fake addresses
  • Asking real customers for honest reviews (correct)

Honest reviews build prominence.
keyPoints: Local ranking depends on relevance, distance and prominence.
Keep profile details consistent and earn honest reviews.

topics.title: Trust, quality and staying safe
topics.html:
Search engines look for signs that a site is reliable, especially for topics that affect health, money or safety. These signs are often summarised as experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness.

Showing trust on a page
SignalExample
Who wrote itAn author name and a short real biography
Why they knowQualifications or direct experience
Where it comes fromLinks to sources and dates
How to contactA real address, phone number and email
SafetyHTTPS and clear privacy information

Staying out of trouble

  • Never copy content; always add something original.
  • Do not hide text or links from visitors.
  • Do not promise or buy rankings.
  • Keep up with official guidance from the search engines.
  • Be patient: SEO normally takes months, not days.
Tip

If a tactic would embarrass you if the search engine's staff explained it to your customers, do not use it.

Check what you just learned

1. SEO results typically take:
  • Weeks to months (correct)
  • Minutes
  • One hour
  • They never come

Rankings build slowly.

Key terms: flip and sort

Backlink
A link from another site
Anchor text
The clickable words of a link
Local pack
The map and nearby businesses in results
Review
A customer's public rating and comment
Penalty
A loss of rankings for breaking the rules
keyPoints: Show who wrote the page, why they know and where facts come from.
Avoid shortcuts; SEO takes months.

modules.title: Measure and improve
modules.summary: Read the reports, spot opportunities and report to a client or owner.
modules.outcome: You can read click-through and ranking reports, find quick wins and write a short audit.
modules.intro: SEO is a loop: measure, change, measure again. The free search console and analytics tools give you most of what you need.

topics.title: Key reports and metrics
topics.html:
Core metrics
MetricMeaningWhere
ImpressionsTimes your page appeared in resultsSearch console
ClicksTimes it was clickedSearch console
CTRclicks / impressionsSearch console
Average positionTypical rank for the queriesSearch console
SessionsVisits to your siteAnalytics
ConversionsVisitors who did what you wantedAnalytics
Formula · Click-through rate

CTR = clicks / impressions

If a page appears 12,000 times and gets 300 clicks, CTR is 2.5%.

These shares are illustrative and vary by query and result layout, but the pattern is real: the top places get far more clicks than the rest.

Check what you just learned

1. CTR is calculated as:
  • Impressions / clicks
  • Clicks / impressions (correct)
  • Position / clicks
  • Sales / clicks

Share of appearances that were clicked.
keyPoints: Impressions, clicks, CTR and position tell the search story.
Conversions tell the business story.

topics.title: Finding quick wins
topics.html:
Three easy-to-find opportunities

  1. Pages on the first page with a low click-through rate: rewrite the title and description.
  2. Pages in positions 8 to 20: improve and expand the content, add internal links.
  3. Pages with many impressions but few clicks for a specific query: check the intent.
Worked example

Using the lab

A page ranks at position 5.2 with a CTR of 2.5%.

  1. It appears often and is near the top, but few click.
  2. The title may be dull or may not match the intent.
  3. Rewrite the title with the benefit and test it for a few weeks.

Answer. A better title can raise clicks without any ranking change.

Common mistakes

  • Changing many things at once, so you cannot tell what worked.
  • Judging the results after a few days.
  • Chasing total traffic instead of conversions.
Tip

Keep a change log with dates. When something moves, you will know what you did before it.

Check what you just learned

1. A page at position 6 with low CTR most likely needs:
  • A new site
  • Deleting
  • A better title and description (correct)
  • More ads

It is visible but unappealing.
keyPoints: Look for high-impression, low-CTR pages and pages just off page one.
Change one thing at a time and log it.

topics.title: Reporting and planning
topics.html:
Prioritising work
PriorityTypical item
High value, low effortFix titles, broken links, big images
High value, high effortNew cornerstone pages, redesign
Low value, low effortMinor cleanups when convenient
Low value, high effortSkip

A good report

  • Starts with a short summary in plain words.
  • Shows two or three numbers that matter to the business.
  • Lists what was done and what it changed.
  • States what comes next and what the owner must decide.
  • Is honest about what is unknown.
Watch out

Avoid reporting only rankings. A first-page ranking for a phrase nobody buys with is worth little.

Check what you just learned

1. Which work should be done first?
  • Low value, high effort
  • Random
  • Neither
  • High value, low effort (correct)

Quick wins first.

Key terms: flip and sort

Impression
One appearance in results
CTR
Click-through rate
Average position
Typical rank
Conversion
A desired action
Audit
A structured review
keyPoints: Prioritise by value and effort.
Report on business results in plain language.

modules.title: SEO in practice
modules.summary: Put it together: plan a project, avoid common myths and keep up with change.
modules.outcome: You can plan a three-month SEO programme, separate myths from facts and keep learning.
modules.intro: SEO is a long game played with changing rules. This final module turns the pieces into a plan and prepares you to keep up.

topics.title: A three-month plan
topics.html:
A starter plan
MonthFocusTypical tasks
1FoundationAudit; fix technical issues; set up search console and analytics; complete the business profile
2ContentKeyword plan; improve top pages; write the first new helpful pages; fix titles
3Authority and reviewEarn links and reviews; add internal links; measure and plan the next quarter

In a short project you cannot expect big movements in rankings for competitive phrases. You can, however, fix problems, improve titles and publish content that begins to earn impressions.

Set expectations honestly

  • Rankings improve gradually over months.
  • Competitive phrases may take a year.
  • Technical fixes show faster than new content.
  • Algorithm updates can change results; focus on durable quality.
Tip

Choose a small set of target pages and a small set of numbers to track, then protect them from distractions.

Check what you just learned

1. What is a sensible month-one focus?
  • Fixing foundations (correct)
  • Buying links
  • Hiding content
  • Copying a rival

Fix technical basics first.
keyPoints: Foundation, content, then authority.
Be honest about timing.

topics.title: Myths and facts
topics.html:
Common myths
MythFact
Keyword stuffing helpsIt makes pages unreadable and can be penalised
More pages always mean more trafficThin pages dilute quality
SEO is a one-off taskIt is ongoing: competitors and engines change
Paid ads improve organic rankThey are separate systems
Meta keywords matterThey are ignored by major engines
Anyone can guarantee page oneNo one controls the engine
Tip

Test claims: if someone says a trick works, ask for the evidence, the date and whether the engine's own guidance agrees.

Check what you just learned

1. Which statement is true?
  • Paid ads boost organic rank
  • SEO is ongoing (correct)
  • Meta keywords drive rank
  • Guarantees are honest

SEO needs continuing attention.
keyPoints: Many popular beliefs are myths.
Rely on official guidance and your own measurement.

topics.title: Ethics, careers and staying current
topics.html:
The best SEO professionals are essentially good communicators and careful analysts. They build sites that people find helpful and that are easy for machines to read.

Staying current

  • Read the official guidance and documentation from the search engines.
  • Follow a few respected industry sources and test claims yourself.
  • Run small experiments on your own sites.
  • Learn the basics of web writing, analytics and page speed.
Roles that use SEO
RoleSEO tasks
Content writerIntent, structure, titles
Web developerSpeed, crawlability, markup
MarketerStrategy, reporting, local SEO
Shop ownerLocal profile, reviews, key pages
Watch out

Do not take shortcuts that hurt other people or break rules: fake reviews, scraped content and hidden text harm users and, in the end, your clients.

Check what you just learned

1. The best foundation for long-term SEO is:
  • Tricks
  • Hidden text
  • Helpful pages that serve people (correct)
  • Bought links

Durable value.

Key terms: flip and sort

Algorithm update
A change to how engines rank
Keyword stuffing
Overusing a phrase
Guideline
Official advice from a search engine
Cornerstone page
A key page on an important topic
keyPoints: Stay current with official guidance and your own tests.
Ethical SEO serves people first.
